page: Microsoft Azure FX24ms_v2 is a high-frequency compute-optimized and memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built on the x86_64 architecture featuring an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The hardware profile allocates 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is exceptionally large for a compute instance at 504.0 GB of RAM, equating to 21.0 GB per vCPU. Cache provisioning is robust, featuring 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for hardware-accelerated matrix operations.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong single-threaded performance driven by the 4.2 GHz clock frequency. The VM achieves strong (top 25%) results in Geekbench single-core testing (2,128.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (34.45 GB/sec), as well as a top-tier (top 10%) score in Geekbench text processing (2,965.0). Multi-core compute performance remains solid within the middle 50% across stress-ng multi-core (26,678.35) and Geekbench multi-core (15,360.0). Small-model CPU LLM inference shows high throughput, reaching 420.68 tokens/sec in text generation (top 10%) on a 135M parameter model. Static web serving throughput also ranks within the top 25% at 46.47 GB/sec.

Regarding storage and network connectivity, the FX24ms_v2 does not bundle any local storage, requiring attached network storage disks such as Azure Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators are absent, with a GPU count of zero, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provided. Memory throughput testing shows adequate uncached read bandwidth of 117.18 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 54.55 GB/sec, although the PassMark memory benchmark reflects lower efficiency (weak category at 1,789.98).

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX24ms_v2 combines a high-clock CPU with a heavy memory ratio (over 20 GB per core) without tying up budget in dedicated GPU hardware. This distinct configuration favors workloads constrained by per-core licensing fees, in-memory computing, EDA tooling, financial modeling, and memory-bound databases that demand top-tier single-threaded compute capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure FX24ms_v2 is a high-clock, compute-optimized virtual machine equipped with an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs (12 physical cores) and an expansive 504.0 GB of RAM, it delivers 21.0 GB of memory per core alongside a substantial 260 MB L3 cache and AMX matrix instructions. It bundles no local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Benchmark testing shows strong single-core performance, excelling in single-thread compression, text processing, and small-model CPU LLM text generation. While multi-threaded compute and uncached memory bandwidth maintain solid mid-tier output, its combined high-frequency execution and extensive memory density make it especially suited for memory-intensive enterprise databases, electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, and applications bound by core-based software licensing.
